answer: Sequential Physical Challenge Chain. Each identity must solve a fresh challenge whose answer depends on hardware timing noise from a falcon-class FPGA board, signed and chained to the prior block. An atlas of past challenge outputs is published, so duplicates are rejected instantly. The crystal oscillator drift inside each board makes replay across devices infeasible. An attacker cannot fake one operator's timing signature at scale; each new identity costs a distinct physical board plus rack time, roughly $400 and hours of setup.
